claims.quote: Evidence from the New Contract, a pro-worker AI campaign organisation, reveals that the public are deeply suspicious about AI. Around six in 10 people expect the gains to flow to wealthy investors and big corporations, while just 7% think they will be shared fairly across our society.
claims.claim: Around six in ten people expect AI's gains to go mainly to wealthy investors and big corporations, and only 7% think they will be shared fairly.
claims.source_name: Evidence from the New Contract (figures matching KCL/Opinium survey on public attitudes to AI and work)
claims.source_org: The New Contract; underlying survey by King's College London (Opinium fieldwork)
claims.source_notes: Speaker names the New Contract; no New Contract publication was found. The six-in-ten and 7% figures match the King's College London study published 19 May 2026 (fieldwork 16-29 April 2026), so dated to that original publication as a re-shared figure. The New Contract item may be later.
claims.vintage_rationale: Matches the May 2026 KCL survey; no newer edition found before the July 2026 debate.

claims.quote: Understandably, seven in 10 workers are worried about the impact of AI on their jobs.
claims.claim: Seven in ten UK workers are worried about the impact of AI on their jobs.
claims.source_name: Evidence from the New Contract (figures matching KCL/Opinium survey on public attitudes to AI and work)
claims.source_org: The New Contract; underlying survey by King's College London (Opinium fieldwork)
claims.source_notes: Attribution to the New Contract inferred from the paragraph it sits in. KCL reports 69% of workers worried about the economic impact of AI job losses, but only 38% worried about their own job.
claims.vintage_rationale: The 69% figure is about the economic impact of AI job losses in general; the same survey found only 38% of workers worried about their own job, so 'their jobs' overstates it.

claims.quote: Even the Foreign Secretary said recently that AI poses a Hiroshima-style threat to humanity unless global rules are put in place.
claims.claim: The UK Foreign Secretary has said AI poses a Hiroshima-style threat to humanity unless global rules are agreed.
claims.source_name: Yvette Cooper's Chatham House essay and Guardian interview warning of an 'AI Hiroshima'
claims.source_notes: Reported 6 July 2026 (essay and interview published around 5-6 July). Cooper's words were 'We cannot afford to wait for an AI equivalent of Hiroshima before we act.'
claims.vintage_rationale: A statement made two days before the debate; fairly reported.

claims.claim: Australia has about 165 data centres, with about 225 in the pipeline.

claims.quote: right now in New South Wales data centres use around one per cent of water. In the next 10 years, this is projected to increase to 25 per cent of Sydney's water.

claims.source_notes: Reuters report (15 Sep 2025, republished by RNZ) gives Sydney Water's forecast of up to a quarter of Sydney's available water by 2035. Sydney Water figures describe the current share as under 1% of Greater Sydney demand, not NSW. The forecast was repeated in 2026.
claims.vintage_rationale: The main proposition is a projection to 2035.
